Failures
ask-claude-fixed.title:
Before I refactor the upload path I need to know how you want failures handled.

The current code retries three times with a fixed delay, swallows the last error and marks the file as uploaded anyway, which is why the Files pane sometimes shows files that never reached storage. A second problem: the retry loop holds the request open for up to 45 seconds, so the browser times out first and retries on its own, which doubles every upload under load.

Which behaviour do you want for the refactored path, keeping in mind that the mobile client cannot show a progress bar?
options: 1 | Retry with backoff (Recommended) | Retry five times with exponential backoff starting at 200 ms, then surface the error to the caller and leave the file unmarked
2 | Fail fast | Report the first error to the user immediately and never retry on the server side
3 | Queue and retry later | Accept the upload into a durable queue, answer 202 at once and retry in the background with a dead-letter list
4 | Keep the current behaviour | Leave the retry loop as it is and only fix the false 'uploaded' mark
